skill.name: nansen-token-research
skill.description: Guides token research with the Nansen CLI, including token info, OHLCV data, holders, flows, DEX trades, PnL, and perpetuals views.
skill.summary: Run structured Nansen CLI workflows for deep token research.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are false positives from Markdown inline code and fenced command examples in SKILL.md. The API key findings declare required configuration, not hardcoded secrets. A semantic finding notes the broad Bash(nansen:*) tool allowance and recommends narrowing the command surface.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed-tools to documented nansen research token subcommands when the platform supports narrower Bash patterns.
Document that NANSEN_API_KEY must be set only in the environment and never pasted into prompts or files.
State that results depend on Nansen API support and may expose queried token addresses to Nansen.

static_findings.snippet: `--chain` required for spot endpoints. Use `--token <address>` for token-specific endpoints.
`flow-intelligence` breaks down by label: whales, smart traders, exchanges, fresh wallets, public fi
| `--chain` | Required for spot endpoints (ethereum, solana, base, etc.) |
| `--symbol` | Token symbol for perp endpoints (e.g. BTC) |
- `holders --smart-money` returns UNSUPPORTED_FILTER for tokens without SM tracking.
- `flow-intelligence` may return all-zero flows for illiquid tokens.

semantic_findings.title: Broad CLI Tool Allowance
semantic_findings.description: The skill grants Bash(nansen:*) in allowed-tools, which allows any nansen CLI command rather than only token research subcommands. This broadens execution and external API access beyond the documented workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowlist is explicit in SKILL.md, and the documented commands need nansen CLI execution. The risk is scope breadth, not evidence of malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Token analysts need repeatable commands for deep onchain and market research. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Nansen CLI workflows for holders, flows, trades, PnL, and perps.
actual_capabilities: Shows commands for token info and OHLCV research by token address and chain.
Guides holder analysis, including smart-money holder filters when supported.
Provides commands for token flows, flow intelligence, and bought-sold activity.
Supports DEX trade, PnL, perpetual trade, position, and leaderboard queries.
Lists flags for chains, tokens, symbols, timeframes, sorting, fields, tables, and CSV output.
limitations: Requires the nansen CLI to be installed and available to the agent.
Requires NANSEN_API_KEY to be configured by the user.
Only covers Nansen token research commands documented in SKILL.md.
Results depend on Nansen API availability, chain support, and token liquidity.

use_cases.title: Review Token Holder Quality
use_cases.description: Use Nansen holder and smart-money commands to compare wallet concentration and tracked holder groups.

use_cases.title: Trace Recent Token Flows
use_cases.description: Use flow, flow intelligence, and bought-sold commands to study recent movement across labels and wallets.

use_cases.title: Check Trading and Perp Activity
use_cases.description: Use DEX trade, PnL, perp trades, positions, and leaderboard commands before drafting a market brief.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Token Snapshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the nansen-token-research skill to gather token info and 1h OHLCV for <token_address> on solana. Summarize key observations.

prompt_templates.title: Holder and Flow Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Research <token_address> on <chain>. Compare holders, smart-money holders when available, seven-day flows, and flow intelligence labels.

prompt_templates.title: Trading Activity Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze <token_address> on <chain>. Review recent DEX trades and PnL sorted by total PnL. Note unusual trader behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-Market Token Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a token research brief for <token_address> on <chain> and <symbol> perps. Include holders, flows, DEX trades, PnL, perp positions, and risks.

output_examples.input: Research a Solana token for holder and flow signals.
output_examples.output: A brief that lists holder concentration, smart-money availability, recent token flows, label breakdowns, and caveats for unsupported filters.

output_examples.input: Compare trading behavior for a token across spot and perps.
output_examples.output: A market note covering DEX activity, profitable wallets, perp positions, leaderboard signals, and open research questions.

output_examples.input: Prepare data points for a token research memo.
output_examples.output: A structured summary of token info, price intervals, holder groups, flow intelligence, PnL leaders, and liquidity limitations.

best_practices: Confirm the token address, chain, and symbol before running commands.
Start with token info and OHLCV before deeper holder, flow, or PnL queries.
Treat illiquid-token and unsupported-filter messages as research caveats.
anti_patterns: Do not paste private API keys into prompts or command arguments.
Do not assume smart-money filters are available for every token.
Do not use token symbols for spot endpoints that require token addresses.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Nansen account?
faq.answer: Yes. The nansen CLI must be installed and configured with NANSEN_API_KEY.

faq.question: Can it research any chain?
faq.answer: It uses chains supported by Nansen and the installed CLI. The examples include solana, ethereum, and base.

faq.question: Does it place trades?
faq.answer: No. It only guides research commands for analytics views.

faq.question: Can it export data?
faq.answer: The documented flags include table output, field selection, and CSV formatting.

faq.question: How should I handle API keys?
faq.answer: Set NANSEN_API_KEY in the environment. Do not paste the key into prompts or shared files.

faq.question: What are common data caveats?
faq.answer: Some smart-money filters may be unsupported. Flow intelligence can return all-zero flows for illiquid tokens.
